add_hint: Single mode: `"hint created: <id>"`. Batch mode: `{ids: [...], errors?: {...}}`; `ids` holds 0 for a failed item and `errors` is keyed by item index.
add_intent: Batch mode: `{ids: [...], errors?, skipped?: [{index, summary, existing_id, existing_state}], open_intents?: [{id, summary, priority}], note?}`; `ids` holds 0 for an intent skipped as a duplicate of an open or running one. Single mode: `"intent created: <id>"`, or the batch shape when the intent was skipped or other unclaimed open intents exist.
add_task_scope: `{added: [{kind, value}, ...], errors?: {...}}`; `errors` is keyed by entry index.
cancel_intent: `"intent <id> cancelled"`. The intent records the canceller's holder label as `cancelled_by`. Errors with the holder label and expiry if another session has a live claim on the intent.
complete_intent: `"intent <id> marked done"`, followed by a reminder to call `start_intent` first when the intent was never started. The intent records the completer's holder label as `completed_by`. Errors with the holder label and expiry if another session has a live claim on the intent.
engagement_status: `{task_id, exploration_id, goal, status, findings_total, facts_total, frontier_open, done_intents, coverage: {entries, gaps}}`. `status` is `open`, or `achieved` once `goal_met` has run.
enrich_domain: `{facts?: [{parent, text, source}], assets?: [{type, value}]}`. Facts are DNS records (`A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `NS`, `TXT`) and reverse-DNS results; assets are discovered IPs and CNAME subdomains.
enrich_ip: `{facts?: [{parent, text, source}], assets?: [{type, value}]}`. Facts are PTR records; assets are the discovered hostnames as subdomains.
enrich_service: `{facts?: [{parent, text, source}], assets?: [{type, value}]}`. Facts cover status code, final redirect target, technology headers, page title, meta generator and TLS certificate details (CN, issuer, expiry, SANs); assets are non-wildcard SANs as subdomains.
export_engagement: JSON: `{version, exported_at, goal, description, nodes, edges, constraints, assets, findings, credentials, coverage, scope, company_id?, companies?: [{id, name, logo?, scope: [{kind, value, raw, reason?}]}], target_changes?}`. CSV: `{format, exported_at, assets_csv, findings_csv, nodes_csv}`.
generate_report: Markdown report as text, with a Target changes section when any were recorded.
graph_overview: `{task: {description, goal}, goals?, hints?, open_intents?, running_intents?, recent_done_intents?, done_intents_total, frontier_open, findings_total, findings_dismissed, findings_merged, facts, finding_list?, recent_facts?, coverage: {entries, gaps}, task_credentials?: [{id, domain, username, source, note}], changes_cursor, unrestored_target_changes?}`. Node entries carry `id`, `state` and their payload fields; `recent_done_intents` and `recent_facts` hold the last 10. Running intents carry `claimed_by` (a holder label) and `claim_expires_at`; open intents whose claim lapsed carry `claim_expired` and `previous_owner`. Pass `changes_cursor` to `list_changes`. `unrestored_target_changes` lists target changes nobody has restored to their baseline yet.
insert_assets: `{results: [{index, id, type}], errors: [{index, error}]}`; `index` is the position in `assets`. Either list is `null` when empty. Out-of-scope assets land in `errors`.
list_activity: JSON: `{count, activity: [{id, exploration_id, node_id?, worker?, kind?, tool?, is_error?, summary?, detail?, created_at}, ...]}`. CSV: the same entries as CSV text.
list_assets: `{count, assets: [{id, type, label, data?}, ...]}`; `count` is the total match count, not the page size.
list_changes: `{session, cursor, count, truncated, note?, my_claims: [{node_id, claim_expires_at, expired?, payload?}], findings?, facts?, intents?, goals?, hints?, assets?, unrestored_target_changes?}`. `session` is your own holder label, the value other agents see in `claimed_by`. Each change carries `change` (`new` or `updated`) and `changed_at`; running intents carry `claimed_by` (a holder label) and `claim_expires_at`, or `claim_expired`. Without an identity, an MCP session or `owner`, `session` and `my_claims` are replaced by `claims_error`. `unrestored_target_changes` (present when any exist) lists recorded target changes not yet restored to their baseline: `[{id, target, resource, kind, baseline, baseline_change_id, recorded_by, recorded_at, intent_id?, last_observed?, restore_attempts?}]`.
list_coverage_gaps: `{untargeted_assets, unresolved_intents, unproven_goals, unenriched_services}`. Asset lists hold `{id, type, label, data?}`; node lists hold `{id, kind, state, payload?, origin?}`.
list_engagements: Array of engagement summaries, each with `id`, `goal`, `description`, `status`, `exploration_id`, `created_at`, `node_count`, `finding_count`, `asset_count`, `goals_met`, and `active` flag.
list_evidence: `{count, evidence: [{id, finding_id, kind, filename, size, sha256, created_at}, ...]}`.
list_findings: Array of `{id, summary, vulnclass?, severity?, state?, status?, dismissed?, dismiss_reason?, merged_into?, traffic_count?}`.
list_sessions: `{count, sessions: [{label, self, created_at, last_active, context}, ...], identities: [{name, self, last_active}, ...]}`. `label` is the hashed holder label the session's claims show in `claimed_by` when taken without `owner` (raw session IDs are never returned); `self` marks the caller's own session. `identities` lists the `X-Artex-Identity` names that made requests to this server process within the claim lease; clients on protocol 2026-07-28 have no session and appear only there.
list_untested_assets: `{assets: [{id, type, label, data?}, ...], total, page, page_size}`.
merge_findings: `{id, vulnclass, name, severity, summary, evidence, asset_ids, status, requested_primary_id?, skipped?: [{id, reason}]}`. `requested_primary_id` is set when the requested primary was already merged and `id` is the live finding it resolved to.
prove_goal: `"goal <id> marked met"` (or `"goal <id> marked met; all goals of this task are met"`).
record_fact: Single fact: `"fact created: <id>"`. Multiple facts: `{ids: [...], errors?: {...}}`; `ids` holds 0 for a failed item and `errors` is keyed by item index.
record_target_change: `{change_id, target, resource, kind, baseline, baseline_change_id, recorded_by, identity_error?}`. When unrestored changes on the same target and resource already exist, also `warning`, `original_matches_baseline` and `existing_changes: [{id, target, resource, kind, baseline, baseline_change_id, original_fingerprint, recorded_by, recorded_at, backup?, intent_id?, last_observed?, restore_attempts?, yours?}]`; `baseline` is then the first recorded original fingerprint, not yours.
record_target_restore: `{results: [{change_id, target, resource, status, observed, baseline, baseline_change_id, also_restored?, message}], all_restored, unrestored_target_changes, identity_error?}`. `status` is `restored` (observed matched the baseline), `not_restored` (mismatch, recorded as an attempt) or `already_restored`; `unrestored_target_changes` counts the engagement's remaining unrestored changes.
report_finding: `{finding_id, node_id, possible_duplicates?: [{id, vulnclass, severity, summary}], duplicate_note?}`. `possible_duplicates` lists open findings in this engagement with the same vulnclass (ignoring case, punctuation and common long forms such as "Insecure Direct Object Reference" for `idor`) on an overlapping asset or where either names no asset, or with the same severity on an overlapping asset; merge any that are the same issue with `merge_findings`. Pass `node_id` as `evidence_id` to `prove_goal`.
set_constraints: Single mode: `"constraint created: <id>"`. Batch mode: `{ids: [...], errors?: {...}}`; `ids` holds 0 for a failed item and `errors` is keyed by item index.
set_goals: `{created: [{id, text, state}], skipped?: [{text, reason, existing_id?}], existing_goals?: [{id, text, state}], note?, errors?}`. `reason` is `duplicate` (same text as `existing_id`, ignoring case and whitespace) or `goals_already_set`: the engagement already had goals and `append` was not true, so nothing was added and `existing_goals` lists them.
start_intent: `"intent <id> is now running; claimed by <label> until <time>"` (`renewed` when the caller already held the claim). `<label>` is the caller's identity name (with a hashed suffix when `owner` is passed) or otherwise a hash of the holder, never its session ID or `owner`. Errors with the holder label and expiry if another holder has a live claim, asks for `owner` when the connection has neither an identity nor an MCP session, and refuses callers without a verified identity when the server requires one.
traffic_get: Text with `--- REQUEST ---` and `--- RESPONSE ---` sections, each clipped at 32 KiB, preceded by a `REWRITTEN by rule ids [...]` line when rewrite rules changed the exchange.
traffic_messages: `{total, messages: [{seq, direction, type, size, payload, event?, blob?, truncated?}, ...]}`.
traffic_patterns: `{top_paths: [{path, count}], error_hosts: [{host, total, codes_4xx, codes_5xx, status_samples}], new_endpoints: [{host, path, first_ts, count}]}`.
traffic_stats: `{total_exchanges, unique_hosts, status_codes, methods, top_hosts: [{host, count}], earliest_ts?, latest_ts?, avg_resp_size, avg_req_size, total_req_bytes, total_resp_bytes}`.
